title: Held, Not Touched
logline: A gem-cutter brings a rough stone close under a single lamp and looks at it for far longer than seems reasonable, until both its flaws and its worth become visible.
human_question: What changes when attention stops scattering and stays on one thing for a long time?

situation.what_happens: A cutter takes in a rough stone and decides what it will become. Most of the work is looking: the stone turned under light, set down, picked up again, while the room is ignored. A wrong angle destroys value that cannot be recovered, so the decision is deferred until the looking has produced it. Then the cutting is quick, and the stone leaves.
situation.who_is_involved: The cutter, working on commission or on their own stock; the owner of the stone, who is carrying the risk; the buyer or broker at the other end; apprentices or family who work in the same room.
situation.what_is_at_stake: Real money, other people's money, and a reputation that rests on judgement. For the film: the temptation to claim that skilled concentration is the same thing as the meditative absorption the texts describe, which the sources explicitly deny.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A stone arrives with a history and an expectation attached. The pressure builds as the decision is delayed and the owner waits. It ends in a cut that is either right or wrong, and the market says which. Reality decides the value, and whether the cutter is willing to say anything about how the looking feels.

concept_merge.why_together: C013 (the fine-material minds) contributes the sources' own image for deep concentration: someone who wants to really know an object brings it close, stops looking elsewhere, and looks long at its colours and marks until it is completely clear [C013-P:L48–L52]. C099 (the absorption process) contributes what the texts count as skill, which is not intensity but control: being able to turn to it, enter, stay, leave on time and look back over it at will [C099-P:L69–L79]. C031 (the factors in absorbed minds) contributes the texts' analysis of what such a state actually consists of, which is a precise set of factors, some dropping away in a fixed order as it deepens.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Together they make visible both the attraction and the limit of the comparison. Long, controlled, undistracted looking is filmable and real, and it is what the sources reach for when they want to explain themselves; but the sources also say a craftsman's absorption can only ever be an echo of what they mean, because their subject is defined by which factors are present, not by how well the work goes. The film can hold the echo without claiming the thing.

concept_links.why: The Pradeepika explains deep concentration by exactly this behaviour: bringing an object close, shutting out the room and looking for a long time until everything about it is plain [C013-P:L48–L52]. The digest is explicit that absorption is not 'flow' or being in the zone at work, so the film keeps this as the source's working image and makes no claim about the cutter's mind.

The digest treats real skill as being able to turn toward the object, enter, stay, leave on time and review [C099-P:L69–L79], and states that a craftsman's absorption can only be an echo or analogy, never an instance. That is precisely the register the film works in.

The texts describe a settled mind by counting what accompanies it, and say the drop-outs follow a set order tied to absorption factors, with one of the most refined moments also one of the richest. The digest warns that this is an analytic count, not something a person could feel or a camera could see, and that work focus is not these states. The link is background for the film's restraint rather than something the images can carry; it is the weakest link in this idea and could move to the film about deepening by subtraction.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Ordinary attention only brushes past things, but attention that stays on one thing for a long time begins to see it clearly. The texts picture someone bringing an object close and looking at it until everything about it is plain.
what_must_be_real: The cutter's actual trade, actual commission and actual risk. The film never says the cutter is meditating, is absorbed in the sense the texts mean, or has attained anything.
position_hint: middle: it follows the film about choosing a practice by showing what long attention on one object looks like from outside, before the group moves on to depth and to insight.
risks: Overclaiming a meditative state for ordinary skilled work, which both digests rule out
Trade secrecy about value, sourcing and labour conditions in the gem trade
Becoming a craft showcase with nothing at stake
drop_if: No cutter will let a real commission be followed from rough stone to sale
The film could only work by asking the cutter to perform stillness

connections.note: Two close studies of attention refining: one on a single object, one across a graduated sequence.

selection.reason: Used by EPD-0089; the C013 image is the source's own, with the flow-state misreading explicitly blocked.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
